result: Tie at 11 out of 20 between First‑year EE students overwhelmed by lecture density, Second‑year EE students preparing for mid‑term exams, Senior EE students needing project cheat sheets. No narrower opportunity was picked, so the founder's own idea is kept.
scale: 1 no sign, 3 some sign, 5 strong sign; pain, willingness to pay and reach are given by the model from the Phase 1 evidence

scores.reason: Sourced evidence shows first‑year EE students struggle with lecture density and need efficient note‑taking, indicating high pain; no pay sources exist, so willingness to pay is low; the target market is large and accessible, giving high reach.
scores.title: First‑year EE students overwhelmed by lecture density

scores.reason: Sourced evidence indicates second‑year EE students need concise revision notes for mid‑terms, showing high pain; no pay sources, so willingness to pay is low; the student population is sizable and reachable.
scores.title: Second‑year EE students preparing for mid‑term exams

scores.reason: Sourced evidence shows senior EE students need quick reference cheat sheets for projects, indicating high pain; no pay sources, so willingness to pay is low; the target group is reachable through university channels.
scores.title: Senior EE students needing project cheat sheets

founder_fit_basis: computed from the brief: the founder has none of the needed skills (writing, web development, design)
pick_rule: highest total, added up by code; a tie is reported as a tie and keeps the founder's own idea

smallest_version.value: A lightweight website that hosts digital notes, summaries, and cheat sheets for electrical engineering undergraduates.
